arguments.premise_synthesis: Over different periods, asset classes like stocks and gold alternate in relative performance. Rebalancing forces selling the overvalued asset and buying the undervalued one relative to the target allocation, and this approach works even when both assets are rising over the long term. By adhering to a fixed allocation across three to five uncorrelated asset classes and periodically rebalancing, investors can systematically buy low and sell high without needing to time the market.
arguments.conclusion_supported: Rebalancing between uncorrelated asset classes, when applied systematically, allows investors to capitalize on relative performance fluctuations and improve portfolio outcomes without market timing.
